prompt_name: College Coach Contact Database — Monthly-Sync Build Spec
role: You are a senior software engineer. Build a production system that maintains a living master database of college sport coaches and their contact information, updated from a CSV file each month, with automatic change detection and a monthly movement report. Follow this specification exactly. Ask before inventing schema not described here.
objective: Ingest a monthly CSV per sport/division, reconcile it against the existing master database, automatically apply contact-info updates and coaching-movement changes (hires, departures, program changes, promotions), and produce (a) the refreshed master data and (b) a separate monthly 'Movement' report summarizing every program that had a change that month.

scope.sports_future: Architecture must be sport-agnostic; adding a sport must require only new CSV ingestion, no schema change.

inputs.file_format: CSV, one file per (sport, division). Header row present. UTF-8.
expected_columns: institutional_context (optional, pass-through): City, Region, Size of city, Private/Public, Religious affiliation, HBCU/CommunityCollege/WomenOnly, Average GPA, SAT ranges, ACT range, Acceptance rate, Total yearly cost, Majors offered, No. of undergrads, U.S. News rankings, IPEDS/NCES ID

optional_vendor_change_flags.note: Some source files include per-row change markers. Use them as HINTS, but the authoritative change detection is a diff against the prior master (see change_detection).

flags.Added?: x=new person | j=job change | e=email change | #=phone change
flags.Removed? (y): coach no longer at this program

ingestion_robustness: Auto-detect the real header row (files may have license/notice/metadata rows above it).
Treat '-' and empty cells as null.
Trim whitespace; lowercase and trim emails; normalize phones to (XXX) XXX-XXXX.
Skip rows with no first or last name.
Map incoming columns to the canonical schema by header name, tolerant of extra/missing/reordered columns.

coach.master_id: Stable, permanent, system-generated identifier. NEVER key a coach on email or school (both change when they move). This ID follows the person across job changes.
coach.institutional_context: Store the institutional/academic columns joined by school (do not duplicate per coach in storage; join on program).

coach_history.purpose: Immutable append-only log of every change, powering the monthly Movement report and audit trail.

identity_resolution.goal: Correctly decide whether an incoming CSV row is an EXISTING coach (same person) or a NEW coach, so that a coach who changes schools is tracked as one continuous record, not deleted-and-recreated.
match_order: 1. Exact email match (case-insensitive) to an existing active coach -> same person.
2. Same first+last name AND same school+sport -> same person (contact update).
3. Same first+last name at a DIFFERENT school in the same sport, where the prior school no longer lists them -> same person who MOVED (program_change).
4. Strong fuzzy name match (nickname/spelling variants, e.g. 'Mike'/'Michael', 'Donte''/'Donte') + corroborating signal (same email domain, same twitter handle) -> same person.
identity_resolution.ambiguity: When two plausible matches exist (e.g., two coaches with the same common name), do NOT auto-merge. Flag to a human review queue with both candidates.
identity_resolution.name_changes: Support a coach whose displayed name changes (maiden->married). Prefer email/handle continuity to preserve master_id.

change_detection.method: For each monthly run, diff the incoming file against the current master (authoritative), and reconcile vendor change-flags as hints.

rules.hired: A coach (by identity_resolution) present this month at a program where they were not present last month AND not matched to any departing coach elsewhere.
rules.program_change: An existing coach now appears at a different school (same sport). Record from_school -> to_school; update current_school; keep master_id.
rules.departed: A coach who was active last month is (a) marked Removed, or (b) absent from their program's roster this month and not found at any other program. Set status='departed'. (Note: the raw feed cannot distinguish 'fired' vs 'resigned' vs 'retired'—label as 'departed' unless a reason is provided.)
rules.position_change: Same coach, same school, title changed (e.g., Assistant -> Head Coach). Record from_title -> to_title.
rules.email_change: Same coach, email differs -> update + log.
rules.phone_change: Same coach, phone differs -> update + log.

change_detection.newest_data_wins: The incoming monthly file is treated as the newest truth for contact fields on matched coaches; overwrite stale values and log the change.
change_detection.safety: Provide a config flag to auto-apply high-confidence changes but route low-confidence/ambiguous ones (uncertain identity matches, suspicious mass-departures) to a human review queue before applying.

monthly_movement_report.requirement: Produce a SEPARATE tab/sheet each month summarizing every program that had movement, so the user can see coaching changes at a glance.
monthly_movement_report.grouping: By program (school + sport), then by change.
columns: Change type (Hired | Departed | Moved-In | Moved-Out | Promoted | Contact updated)
From (prior school / prior title / old value)
To (new school / new title / new value)

outputs.primary: Updated master database (per sport/division), with each coach's newest contact info and current program.
export_formats: CSV per sport/division for contact-DB upload
combined workbook (xlsx) with one data tab per division + one Movement tab per month
optional: API/DB for a live app feed
outputs.history: Full coach_history retained so any past month's movement can be regenerated.

data_quality_rules: De-duplicate within a monthly file on email, else name+school.
Validate email syntax; blank malformed addresses (do not fabricate).
Never invent emails/phones/socials; missing stays blank.
Standardize division labels and phone formatting.
Preserve institutional/academic context columns as pass-through, joined by program.
Flag suspicious bulk changes (e.g., an entire conference 'departing' in one month = likely a feed error) for human review rather than auto-applying.

optional_live_verification.purpose: Purchased/monthly feeds lag real-world coaching turnover. Optionally cross-check a coach's email/program against the school's current athletics staff directory to catch changes newer than the feed.
optional_live_verification.behavior: Where a live check contradicts the feed, flag for review; where it fills a blank, propose the value labeled 'verified from athletics site'.

edge_cases: Same person listed at two schools in one month (transition period) -> keep most recent/primary, log the move.
Two different real people with the same name -> do not merge; disambiguate by email/handle/school.
Interim/acting titles -> capture as position; treat interim->permanent as position_change.
Coach returns to a former school after time away -> reuse original master_id if identity matches.
Reordered or added columns in a future monthly file -> map by header name, not position.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest a monthly CSV per sport/division and update the master with zero manual data entry for high-confidence changes.
A coach who moves schools keeps ONE master_id and shows as 'program_change', not delete+create.
Departures, hires, program changes, promotions, and contact updates are each detected and logged.
A monthly Movement tab lists every program with movement and the before/after for each change.
Re-running the same month is idempotent (no duplicate history, no double-applied changes).
Adding a new sport requires only providing its CSV, no code/schema change.
Nothing is fabricated; ambiguous changes are queued for human review, not silently applied.

tech_notes.storage: Relational DB (e.g., Postgres) with tables: coaches, programs, coach_history, ingestion_batches. Or a spreadsheet-based store if kept small.
tech_notes.ingestion: Deterministic pipeline: parse -> normalize -> resolve identity -> diff -> classify changes -> apply(high-confidence)/queue(low-confidence) -> write outputs -> append history.
tech_notes.reproducibility: Every monthly run recorded as a batch with a timestamp so reports and rollbacks are possible.
tech_notes.human_in_the_loop: A lightweight review queue UI for ambiguous identity matches and suspicious bulk changes.
